No interest
if paid in full?

lines.text: "No interest if paid in full" is not 0%.
lines.say: "No interest if paid in full" is not zero percent.

lines.text: Miss the deadline by even $1, and interest gets charged back to the day you bought it.
lines.say: Miss the deadline by even one dollar, and interest gets charged back to the day you bought it.

lines.text: Our math: a $1,200 purchase at 29.99% APR, and you pay $100 a month for 11 months.
lines.say: Our math: a twelve hundred dollar purchase at twenty-nine point nine nine percent A P R, and you pay one hundred dollars a month for eleven months.

lines.text: That leaves $100 when the 12-month promo ends.
lines.say: That leaves one hundred dollars when the twelve-month promo ends.

lines.text: On a true 0% intro card, you've paid $0 interest so far. On the deferred deal, you get billed about $195.
lines.say: On a true zero percent intro card, you've paid zero interest so far. On the deferred deal, you get billed about one hundred ninety-five dollars.

lines.text: That's almost double the $100 you still owed, and after the promo the 0% card only charges interest on that $100.
lines.say: That's almost double the hundred dollars you still owed, and after the promo the zero percent card only charges interest on that hundred.

lines.text: It happens a lot: a 2015 CFPB report found more than 40% of subprime borrowers got hit with that back interest.

lines.text: So read the wording: "if paid in full" means deferred interest, while "0% intro APR" means truly zero for now.

post.title: "No interest if paid in full" is not a 0% APR deal
post.ig:
"No interest if paid in full" is not the same as 0% APR.
Deferred interest builds from the purchase date and gets charged if any balance is left when the promo ends.
Our math: $1,200 at 29.99% APR, $100 left after 12 months = about $195 in back interest. A true 0% intro card: $0 so far.
A 2015 CFPB report found more than 40% of subprime borrowers were charged that back interest. Store cards averaged 31.3% APR in 2024 (CFPB).
Sources: CFPB Consumer Credit Card Market reports (2015, 2025), CFPB consumer guides.
News and education, not financial advice.
